name: June
objective: Grow privates with off-peak pricing and bulk packs (Bandra's biggest gap); stop summer travel lapses with freezes, not discounts; test a private-first intro.
strategy:
Privates Month + Out of Office.

Commercial job: Grow privates with off-peak pricing and bulk packs (Bandra's biggest gap); stop summer travel lapses with freezes, not discounts; test a private-first intro.

Privates: Happy Hour (Zero Hangover, All Glutes) (“Happy hour, but the only thing on tap is a trainer.”). Privates are 6.2% of Kwality's revenue (₹20.1L in 12 months) but only ₹31k at Bandra — the biggest product gap in the portfolio. Quiet-hour pricing uses capacity that is otherwise unpaid.

Privates: Private Practice (“Ten sessions. One trainer who knows your knees better than your physio.”). Bulk private purchase is one of the allowed 25% cases. Kwality's PR1V@TE10 code (39 uses) shows demand; a pack converts one-off buyers into a 6-month relationship.

Renewal: Auto-Reply: Out of Office, Still Squatting (“Auto-reply: I'm on vacation, but my membership isn't lapsing.”). Travel is the main reason members lapse in June–July. Flexibility removes the reason; list price protects the ticket. Virtual privates cost trainer time only.

Newcomer: Shy Girl Starter Pack (“Not a front-row person yet? Start with a private.”). Half of CRM leads never trial (Bandra 1,114 of 2,317; Kenkere 2,053 of 3,217). A private first visit removes the intimidation barrier. No historical data on private-first conversion — this is a test.
notes: Build: 62 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.9L; 68 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹15.8L; 30 winbacks = ₹3.5L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.6L. Offers carry ₹17.0L (59% of target); the rest is business-as-usual. Funnel uses measured rates (lead→trial 51% CRM status, trial→member 26.9%) — not invented lifts.

funnel.dataQuality: lead→trial = CRM 'Trial Completed' status (not attendance-verified); trial→member = trailing measured; see dataGaps
